items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Who I like to call Bravery, initially known as Baby Lawrence

ctx.x: Chuck, could you tell us something about these great stories we heard on the grapevine about what the battle of the taps between Teddy Hale and Baby Lawrence?

Yeah, you see the tap dancer's dream, which was Baby Lawrence and he was discovered by the jazz giant, (unintelligible), Don Redman, Teddy Hale, was really the juvenile of the two, because he was -- he hand't been tap dancing as long as tap dancer's dream. Who I like to call Bravery, initially known as Baby Lawrence, now he was dubbed Baby Lawrence by the show folk during the early nightlife up there, I think it was like the Rhythm Club and that -- that new nightclub they had there, they just opened up Morains,…

was being introduced. And -- but it hadn't got popular, you see? Now as I was saying, Teddy Hale was a personage. See, of a shadow, because he played that role. But he was so happy to learn to make his feet, you know, like tap dance. And they used to go around and like musicians, like they'd have their mouthpiece, you know, and they would get on the stand, the band stand and have a -- what they call sit-in, you see? Well the tap dancers, they figured they could do that too, you see. (Recording interruption) Lot…
